newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish O/N depos low in cash surplus, zloty eases.
newsitem.headline: Polish O/N depos low in cash surplus, zloty eases.

text.p: Polish overnight deposits held low at around 10 percent in morning trade as the market remained overliquid and surpluses on banks' required reserve accounts kept a cap on one-day rates, dealers said.

They said this week's cash inflows would likely keep surpluses on daily positions until the end of the reserve period on September 1, and rates were seen remaining below the last 14-day reverse repo rate of 19.12 percent until then.
"One-day deposits rates are not likely to rebound above the 19 percent level until end of the reserve period," said Krzysztof Czarkowski of BRE SA.

At the 0815 GMT overnight deposits were quoted at 7.0/12.0 percent against 8.0/12.0 percent at the opening and Friday's close at 6.0/8.0 percent. Tomorrow/next deposits were quoted at 14.0/16.5 percent, up at bid from 12.5/17.0 percent on Friday.
Polish T-bill yields are seen falling to around secondary market levels at today's 600 million zloty primary aucton in large demand caused by cash surpluses on the money market.

On the secondary T-bill yields eased slightly in light trade before today's tender. The 52-week T-bill was quoted at 19.50/19.35 percent from Friday's 19.65/19.50 and half-year paper was at 19.25/19.10 percent against 19.30/19.15 on Friday.
The zloty recouped this morning's slight losses sparked by an early currency buying trend and traded around opening levels of 1.80/1.74 percent from the trading band centre.
"Zloty movements were mainly adjustments of the local currency to the dollar's slight easing against the mark in European trade," said Maciej Grabosz from Bank Zachodni SA.
At 0900 GMT, the zloty was at 2.7300/20 to the dollar, up from 2.7310/45 at opening and 2.7405/25 on Friday.
It was at 1.8475/85 to the mark, down from opening's 1.8455/75 and Friday's 1.8423/28.
